segments.text: The sky is blue because it reflects the ocean. Well, that's not exactly true. The ocean has nothing to do with it.
Sunlight looks white, but it's actually every color mixed together. Red, orange, yellow, green, blue and violet.
Here's the wild part. When sunlight hits the tiny gas molecules in our air, blue light bounces around way more than red. So blue gets scattered all over the sky.
In fact, violet scatters even more. But the sun sends us less of it, and our eyes are better at seeing blue.
At sunset, light has to travel through much more air to reach you. Most of the blue gets scattered away, and only the reds and oranges make it through.
That's not all. On Mars, it's the opposite. The daytime sky is butterscotch, and sunsets are blue.
So the sky isn't reflecting the ocean. It's sunlight bouncing off the air around you.
